documents.t: "Rest day" usually gets interpreted as "do nothing day." But for most people, total inactivity isn't actually the fastest way to recover — light movement is. Active recovery, done outdoors, tends to outperform the couch in nearly every way that matters: soreness, mood, and how ready you feel for your next real effort.
documents.s: Active Recovery: Why Your Rest Days Should Still Get You Outside

documents.t: Active recovery is low-intensity movement on days you'd otherwise train hard or not at all — think an easy walk, a gentle bike ride, light stretching, or a slow neighborhood loop. The goal isn't to build fitness; it's to keep blood flowing to tired muscles, which helps clear metabolic byproducts faster than sitting still does. This isn't a license to turn rest days into training days. The intensity should feel noticeably easier than your normal effort — if you're breathing hard or your legs are burning, that's not recovery, that's just another workout.

Indoor recovery — a foam roller and a couch — handles the physical side reasonably well. But outdoor active recovery adds something indoor routines don't: a change of environment and light sensory input that's been linked to faster mental recovery from training stress, not just physical recovery. Natural light exposure also helps regulate circadian rhythm, which plays a real role in sleep quality — and sleep is arguably the single biggest lever for actual recovery. There's also a simpler explanation: a short outdoor walk is just more pleasant than another fifteen minutes on a foam roller, and the recovery habit you'll actually stick with is the one that doesn't feel like a chore.
documents.s: Why doing it outside specifically helps

documents.t: A 20-30 minute easy walk, ideally somewhere with some greenery, even if it's just a local park. Light mobility work outside — a stretch session on a mat in your backyard or at a trailhead instead of indoors. An easy, flat bike ride at conversational pace, no hills, no pace targets. A slow loop on a familiar trail — not a new, challenging route. Recovery days aren't the time to explore unknown terrain. The common thread: low effort, low stakes, and outside. If you finish feeling more tired than when you started, dial it back further next time.
documents.s: What this looks like in practice

documents.t: Most training plans benefit from one or two active recovery days between harder sessions, rather than a single static rest day. If you're already tracking outdoor activity in MissionPeak, an easy day doesn't need its own special plan — pick a short, flat route you already know, treat it as a recovery walk rather than a workout, and let it be exactly as unambitious as it sounds. Pair it with a Community built around consistency rather than performance, and active recovery stops feeling like an obligation and starts feeling like a normal part of the week — which, for most people, is exactly when habits actually stick.

documents.s: 7 Tips for Your First Few Hikes

documents.t: Starting out on the trail can feel intimidating — gear lists, trail ratings, and seasoned hikers swapping stories about summits can make a short neighborhood loop feel like the wrong place to begin. It isn't. Every experienced hiker started exactly where you are now. Here are seven practical tips to make your first few hikes safer, more comfortable, and more fun.
documents.s: 7 Tips for Your First Few Hikes

documents.t: It's tempting to pick an ambitious trail for your first outing, but a shorter, well-traveled route is the better choice. Aim for something under 4-5 miles with moderate elevation gain. You'll get a feel for pacing, gear, and your own comfort level without overcommitting.
documents.s: 1. Start smaller than you think you should

documents.t: Weather apps tell you what's happening in town, not necessarily on the mountain. Look for trail-specific forecasts or recent trip reports when available, and always check sunset time so you know your hard deadline for getting back.
documents.s: 2. Check the weather — and the trail conditions

documents.t: Temperature swings on the trail are common, especially with elevation changes. A moisture-wicking base layer, an insulating mid-layer, and a packable rain shell will cover most conditions. Cotton is the one fabric to avoid — it holds moisture and stays cold.
documents.s: 3. Wear layers, not just a jacket

documents.t: A common rule of thumb is about half a liter per hour of moderate activity, more in heat or at altitude. Dehydration sneaks up gradually, so don't wait until you're thirsty to drink.
documents.s: 4. Bring more water than feels necessary

documents.t: Share your route and expected return time with a friend or family member before you go. Cell service drops out in a lot of beautiful places, and this simple habit is one of the best safety nets available.

A first-aid kit, a headlamp (even for day hikes — plans change), a map or downloaded offline route, and some emergency snacks take up very little space but solve a disproportionate number of problems.
documents.s: 6. Pack the small things that matter

documents.t: New hikers often try to match the pace of more experienced friends and burn out early. Find a rhythm where you can hold a conversation without gasping for breath. You'll cover more ground comfortably than you would sprinting and resting in cycles. None of this requires expensive gear or technical training — just a bit of preparation and a willingness to start small. Once you've got a few hikes under your belt, use MissionPeak to find local trails, join a Huddle with other hikers, and track your progress as your confidence grows.
documents.s: 7. Go at your own pace — literally

documents.t: One of the easiest ways to talk yourself out of a first hike is to read a "complete gear list" online and realize you own none of it. The good news: a solid day hike needs far less than the internet implies. Here's what's actually worth packing, and what you can safely skip until you know you'll keep doing this.
documents.s: What to Pack for Your First Day Hike (And What You Can Skip)

documents.t: Water — more than you think. A liter for a short hike, more in heat or at elevation. A simple reusable bottle is fine; you don't need a hydration bladder for a 3-mile loop. Snacks with actual calories. Trail mix, a couple of bars, or a sandwich. Hiking burns more than people expect, and low blood sugar makes everything feel harder than it is. A first-aid basics kit. Adhesive bandages, blister pads, gauze, and a small roll of tape cover the vast majority of small-trail mishaps. Pre-made kits the size of a deck of cards exist for exactly this. A map you don't need signal for. A downloaded offline map or a photo of the trailhead board works. Don't rely on cell service for navigation. A layer for weather you're not currently feeling. Even on a warm day, a packable rain shell or light jacket takes up almost no space and solves a lot of "I didn't expect it to get cold at the top" problems. A headlamp, even for a daytime hike. Plans run long more often than people admit. A $10 headlamp is cheap insurance against finishing the last mile in the dark.
documents.s: The essentials that earn their weight every time

documents.t: Sunscreen and a hat. Especially above the treeline or on exposed trails. A whistle. Lightweight and genuinely useful if you need to signal for help. A small trash bag. For your own wrappers, and because trails stay nicer when hikers pack out more than they pack in.
documents.s: Worth bringing, not worth stressing over

documents.t: Trekking poles — helpful on steep or technical terrain, but unnecessary for most beginner-friendly trails. Borrow a pair before buying if you're curious. A dedicated hiking backpack — any comfortable daypack you already own will do for distances under 6-8 miles. Pack weight matters more than pack brand at this stage. GPS devices or satellite communicators — genuinely useful for remote or solo trips later on, but not a first-hike requirement if you're sticking to popular, well-traveled routes. Specialized hiking boots — supportive sneakers or trail runners are fine for moderate terrain. Save the boot investment for when you know you'll be hiking regularly or tackling rougher ground.
documents.s: What you can skip for now

documents.t: A flat 2-mile loop ten minutes from a parking lot doesn't need the same kit as a 9-mile trail with real elevation gain. Before you pack, check the distance, elevation, and how far you'll be from help — Aurora can pull this up for any trail you're considering, so you're packing for the hike you're actually doing, not a worst-case guess. Once you've got the essentials down, the rest of your kit will grow naturally as you figure out what you personally use versus what just adds weight. Start light, pay attention to what you reach for, and adjust from there.
documents.s: The real rule: match your pack to your plan

documents.t: If you've spent any time in the MissionPeak app, you've probably bumped into a Huddle — maybe a Saturday morning trailhead meetup, a casual evening walk, or a multi-day trip someone in your community put together. Huddles are the feature that turns "I should get outside more" into an actual plan with actual people. Here's a closer look at how to get the most out of them.
documents.s: Getting the Most Out of Huddles

documents.t: A Huddle isn't just a calendar invite. It's built around the logistics that usually make group outdoor plans fall apart — who's driving, where exactly to meet, whether it's beginner-friendly, what happens if it rains. Each Huddle carries its own details: activity type, RSVP cutoff, meeting point, and privacy level, so the planning lives in one place instead of scattered across group chats.
documents.s: What makes a Huddle different from just scheduling a hangout

documents.t: Read the details before you request to join. Activity type and difficulty are usually listed up front — a "Hiking" Huddle will surface trail-specific info that a general one won't. Check the privacy level. Public Huddles are open to anyone; Community and Connection Huddles follow the visibility rules of the group hosting them. If you can't find a Huddle you were told about, it may require a connection or community membership first. Use the extras. Carpool coordination and sign-up sheets exist so you're not negotiating logistics in a separate text thread. If the organizer has set them up, use them — it makes the day smoother for everyone.

Be specific in the description. Distance, difficulty, what to bring, and where exactly to park save you from answering the same five questions individually. Set a realistic RSVP cutoff. Giving yourself a day or two of lead time before the event makes it much easier to plan carpools or manage a waiting list if the Huddle fills up. Use participant approval thoughtfully. For anything beyond a casual public walk, reviewing requests before approving them helps you keep the group size and experience level manageable. Send a reminder close to the date. Plans change. A short update the day before — weather, parking, last-minute changes — keeps no-shows down and confusion to a minimum.

The organizers who get the most out of Huddles tend to run them regularly — a standing Saturday hike, a monthly Community meetup — rather than treating each one as a one-time event. It gives people something to plan around, and it's a lot easier to build a Community around a rhythm than around a single isolated outing. Whether you're hosting your first Huddle or your fiftieth, the goal is the same: make it easy for people to show up and easy for you to manage. Browse upcoming Huddles in the app, or check our support guide for the full feature breakdown.
documents.s: Huddles work best as a habit, not a one-off

documents.t: Hiking alone has its appeal, but most people who stick with outdoor activity long-term do it alongside other people. MissionPeak Communities exist for exactly that part of the equation — a way to find a group built around the kind of outdoor activity you actually want more of, instead of trying to assemble one yourself one connection at a time.
documents.s: Finding Your People: A Closer Look at MissionPeak Communities

documents.t: Connections are one-to-one — the people you've individually linked up with on MissionPeak. Communities are group-level: a shared space organized around a theme, activity, location, or shared goal, where everyone in the group can see and join Huddles, share updates, and find each other without needing an individual connection first. Think of it this way: a Connection is a hiking buddy. A Community is the whole local trail-running group that buddy happens to be part of.
documents.s: Communities vs. Connections — what's the difference

documents.t: Discover Huddles you wouldn't otherwise see. Community-level Huddles are visible to all members, which means you find out about a Saturday group hike even if you don't personally know the organizer. Post updates to a group that already shares your interest. Sharing a trip report or a trail condition update lands in front of people who actually want to see it, rather than your full Connections list. Find people at your pace and interest level. Communities can be built around almost anything — a specific trail system, a skill level, a training goal, a region — so the people in them tend to already have something in common with you. Build a recurring rhythm. Communities that run regular Huddles — a standing weekend hike, a monthly meetup — tend to be the ones that turn casual members into regular ones.
documents.s: What you can do inside a Community

documents.t: Browse Communities from the app's discovery tab, filtered by activity type or location. Some are open to join immediately; others — particularly smaller or more focused groups — require an approval step from an admin, similar to how private Huddles work. If a Community is private and you can't find it through search, you'll typically need an invite or a referral from an existing member.

If you've looked and the Community you want doesn't exist yet, you can start one. A few things that tend to separate Communities that grow from ones that stall: A specific focus beats a general one. "Beginner hikers in [your region]" attracts more engaged members than a generic "outdoor enthusiasts" group. Consistency matters more than size. A small Community that runs a Huddle every other week will outlast a large one that posts once and goes quiet. Clear expectations up front. Setting the activity level, pace, and vibe in your Community description filters in the right people and filters out mismatched expectations later.

The research on outdoor activity and consistency is pretty consistent itself: people who do it with others stick with it longer than people who don't. Communities are the feature designed around that exact insight — not just a social add-on, but the part of MissionPeak built to make "I should get outside more" into something you actually do, regularly, with people who want the same thing. Looking for a Community to join, or thinking about starting one? Check out our Communities guide for the full feature walkthrough, including privacy settings and admin tools.
documents.s: Why this matters more than it might seem

documents.t: It's easy to treat "going for a hike" as just another fitness activity — a way to log steps or burn calories. But the benefits of spending time outdoors go well beyond the physical. A growing body of research points to outdoor activity as one of the more reliable, low-cost tools for supporting mental health.
documents.s: Why Time Outdoors Is One of the Best Things You Can Do for Your Mind

documents.t: Moderate aerobic activity — walking, hiking, cycling — triggers the release of endorphins and reduces levels of cortisol, the body's primary stress hormone. Add natural surroundings to that equation, and the effect compounds: studies on "green exercise" consistently show lower self-reported anxiety and rumination after time spent in natural environments compared to the same activity indoors.
documents.s: The mind-body connection isn't just a slogan

documents.t: One of the most persistent myths about outdoor wellness is that it requires big, dramatic effort — a multi-day backpacking trip or a strenuous peak. In practice, the research suggests even short exposures help. A 20-30 minute walk in a park or along a tree-lined trail has been shown to measurably lower stress markers. The goal isn't endurance; it's consistency.
documents.s: You don't need a summit to feel the benefit

documents.t: If you're active regularly, recovery days matter as much as training days. Easy outdoor walks on rest days keep blood flowing to tired muscles without adding strain, and they give you the mental reset that a scroll through your phone usually doesn't.
documents.s: Recovery is part of the routine, not a footnote

documents.t: Anchor it to something you already do. A short walk after lunch or before dinner is easier to sustain than a stand-alone "wellness activity" that competes for its own time slot. Bring a friend, not just a goal. Social connection amplifies the mental health benefits of outdoor time. A regular walking or hiking partner makes consistency much easier. Track how you feel, not just distance. Mood and energy are harder to quantify than steps, but they're often the more meaningful signal of whether your routine is working. Let easy days be easy. A short walk still counts. The cumulative effect of small, regular outdoor time outperforms occasional big efforts.
documents.s: A few ways to build it into your week

documents.t: Aurora, MissionPeak's AI companion, can suggest beginner-friendly trails and activities near you if you're not sure where to start. And joining a Community built around outdoor wellness is a simple way to add the social piece — research suggests that's often the part that makes a habit stick. Time outdoors isn't a cure-all, and it isn't a replacement for professional support when you need it. But as a regular, accessible habit, it's one of the more evidence-backed ways to support your mental health alongside everything else you're doing. If you're navigating a mental health crisis, please reach out to a professional or a trusted person in your life — outdoor time is a complement to that support, not a substitute for it.

MissionPeak is built around outdoor activities — the type of activity you choose shapes what a Huddle looks like, what stats get tracked when you record, and what counts toward a Challenge.

An activity type is the kind of outdoor activity something on MissionPeak is centered around — for example General or Hiking. Activity types show up in a few places: Huddles — choosing an activity type when creating a Huddle enables type-specific features (like trail details for Hiking). Records — recording an activity with a specific type captures type-relevant stats. Challenges — some Challenge goals are tied to a specific activity type. MissionPeak continues to add support for more activity types over time.

Choosing the right activity type helps MissionPeak: Show you the right fields and options when creating a Huddle or recording an activity. Track meaningful, type-specific stats (like elevation gain for a hike). Match you with the right Huddles, Communities, and Challenges for the activities you care about. See About Records for how to record an activity of a given type.
Connect Apple Health to bring your iPhone and Apple Watch activity data into MissionPeak automatically.

The Apple Health integration lets MissionPeak read workout and activity data from Apple Health on iOS. Once connected, activity you've recorded with your iPhone, Apple Watch, or other Apple Health-connected apps can be used as a Record on MissionPeak.
documents.s: What is the Apple Health integration?

documents.t: Records — imported workouts (like distance, duration, and route where available) can be used as Records on MissionPeak. See About Records. Challenges — progress toward a Challenge's goal can be calculated from Apple Health data, in addition to activity recorded directly in the app. See About Challenges.
Go to Settings > Devices & Services. Select Apple Health. Grant the requested permissions in the iOS system prompt. Choose which data types to share with MissionPeak.

Revisit Settings > Devices & Services any time to review what's connected. Disconnect Apple Health to stop new data from syncing. Previously imported activity and Challenge progress isn't removed automatically. You can also manage MissionPeak's permissions directly from the iOS Health app under Sharing > Apps.

Skip manual entry — activity you've already recorded on your iPhone or Apple Watch counts automatically. Keep Challenge progress up to date without opening a second app. Choose exactly which data types to share.

Aurora is your AI-powered outdoor companion in MissionPeak. Whether you're planning your next adventure, looking for activity ideas, or seeking guidance on health and wellness, Aurora is here to assist you every step of the way.

Aurora is an AI assistant built into MissionPeak. It's designed to answer your questions, recommend activities, and help you make the most of your outdoor journey. Think of Aurora as your digital trail buddy — always ready with insights, tips, and suggestions.

Adventure Planning Ask Aurora to suggest trails, hikes, or activities near you. Get recommendations based on difficulty level, duration, or location. Huddle & Community Support Need help organizing a Huddle? Aurora can guide you with best practices. Looking for a group to join? Ask Aurora to point you toward relevant Communities. Inspiration & Motivation Stuck on what to write? Aurora can help you draft Inspirations. Discover health benefits, outdoor tips, and training ideas from Aurora's guidance. Personalized Recommendations Aurora tailors responses based on your interests, activity history, and profile. The more you engage, the better Aurora gets at helping you.

Open the Aurora section in the app from the navigation bar. Type or speak your question — like chatting with a friend. Aurora will respond instantly with helpful answers, suggestions, or links to MissionPeak features.

Aurora makes MissionPeak smarter and more personal. Instead of searching or guessing, you can: Quickly find relevant Huddles, Communities, or Inspirations. Learn how to stay active, healthy, and safe outdoors. Get real-time support in planning your outdoor lifestyle. tip Try starting with simple prompts like "Suggest a beginner-friendly hike near me" or "How do I create a private Huddle?" to see how Aurora can help.
Carpools make it easy to share rides with other MissionPeak users, whether or not you're headed to a Huddle. Coordinate pickup points, split costs, and cut down on the number of cars on the road.

A Carpool is a shared ride organized on MissionPeak. Carpools come in two forms: Independent Carpools — created on their own, not tied to any event. Useful for a regular commute, a group heading to a trailhead, or any shared trip. Huddle Carpools — created as part of a Huddle. When a host enables carpooling for a Huddle, participants can offer or request rides to that specific event. Both forms work the same way once created: drivers offer available seats, and riders request to join.

Independent or event-based Start a Carpool on its own, or attach one to a Huddle you're hosting or attending. Driver & rider roles Offer a ride as a driver with your available seats, pickup point, and departure time. Request a seat as a rider from any open Carpool. Coordination details Share pickup/drop-off locations, timing, and notes with everyone in the Carpool. Cost sharing Drivers can note if they'd like riders to help cover gas or trip costs. Coordination via Messages Each Carpool has its own conversation for drivers and riders to work out pickup details. See About Messages.

Tap the "+" menu in the app. Select Carpool. Choose whether it's independent or linked to a Huddle you're organizing. Add your route, pickup point, departure time, and available seats. Publish so riders can find and request to join.
Find independent Carpools through Explore, or a Huddle's Carpool tab if one is enabled. Review the route, pickup point, and timing. Request a seat — the driver will confirm.
Carpools help you: Save money and cut down on solo drives. Coordinate rides for a Huddle without juggling separate chats. Meet other MissionPeak users headed the same way.
Challenges give you a fun, goal-driven way to stay active on MissionPeak — set a target, track your progress, and see how you stack up, on your own or with others.

A Challenge is a fitness or activity goal you take on over a set period of time — like a distance, step count, or activity streak. Challenges come in two forms: Independent Challenges — personal goals you set and track on your own. Community Challenges — hosted under a Community, so members can join, track progress together, and compare results.

Independent or Community-hosted Start a personal Challenge, or join one hosted by a Community you're part of. Goal types Track distance, activity count, or streaks, depending on the Challenge. Progress can come from activity recorded directly in the app or synced through a connected service. See About Records and About Devices & Services. Progress tracking See your own progress update as you log qualifying activities. Group participation Community Challenges let members see how the group is progressing together.

Tap the "+" menu in the app. Select Challenge. Choose whether it's independent or hosted under a Community you manage. Set the goal type, target, and duration. Publish so others can join (if hosted under a Community).

Find Community Challenges through the Community's page, or start your own independent Challenge. Tap Join and start logging qualifying activities. Track your progress toward the goal from the Challenge page.
Challenges help you: Stay motivated with a clear, trackable goal. Push yourself independently or alongside your Community. Turn everyday activity into friendly, shared progress.

Communities are where friendships grow, passions unite, and activities thrive on MissionPeak. Whether you're joining a hiking group, starting a local club, or building a space for your close friends, Communities give you the platform to connect and organize around shared interests.

A Community is a group of people who come together on MissionPeak to share common interests, organize Huddles, post content, and build lasting connections. Communities can be small and private (like a close group of friends) or large and public (like a regional hiking club). Think of Communities as your virtual basecamp — a place where members gather, plan, and inspire each other.

Shared space for activities Post updates, discussions, inspirations, and upcoming Huddles. Bring like-minded people together in one organized place. Flexible privacy levels Public – anyone can view posts, Huddles, and other items. Protected – anyone can find the Community and see its overview, but only members see posts, Huddles, and other items. Private – only members can see posts, Huddles, and other items. See Community Privacy Options for full details, including how privacy can be changed after a Community is created. Events & Huddles integration Host Community-specific Huddles and events. Privacy and participation rules automatically follow the Community's settings. Member management Community creators and admins can approve requests, remove members, or assign roles. Members can invite others (depending on Community settings). Inspiration sharing Members can write and share Inspirations (articles, stories, tips) with the group. Great for documenting trips, sharing advice, or motivating others. Topic-based discussions Members can start and join focused, topic-based conversations within the Community. See About Messages.
Tap the "+" menu in the app. Select Community. Give your Community a name, description, and photo. Choose the privacy level (Public, Protected, or Private). Publish and start inviting members.

Discover Communities through the Explore page or search by activity/interest. Review the Community description to see if it's right for you. Tap Join: Instantly join if it's Public. Send a request if it's Protected. Get invited if it's Private.

Communities help you: Find your tribe — people who share your interests. Organize and grow beyond one-off events. Access a steady stream of posts, Huddles, and Inspirations. Build meaningful, long-term connections.

Connections help you build your social circle on MissionPeak by following and engaging with people who inspire you. Whether it's friends, fellow hikers, or outdoor influencers, Connections make it easy to stay updated with their activities and share your own journey.

A Connection is simply the relationship between you and another user on MissionPeak. You can: Follow someone to see their posts, Huddles, and Inspirations in your newsfeed. Be followed by others who want to stay updated with what you share. Connections create a dynamic network of outdoor enthusiasts, making it easier to discover events, communities, and inspiring stories.

Followers – These are people who follow you. They'll see your public or shareable posts, Huddles, and Inspirations in their feed. Following – These are the people you've chosen to follow. Their activities will appear in your feed. This works similar to other social platforms: you don't need mutual approval to follow someone (unless their profile is private).

Personalized newsfeed Following people tailors your feed with their updates. Stay inspired by influencers, trailblazers, and your friends' journeys. Discovery of activities See the Huddles and Communities your Connections are part of. Get recommendations for events and people to follow. Privacy & control You decide who can follow you based on your account privacy settings. You can remove a follower at any time. Influence building The more followers you have, the greater your reach. Great for trail leaders, community builders, or anyone looking to inspire others. Direct messaging Message any of your Connections directly. See About Messages.
Go to a user's profile. Tap Follow. You'll now see their activities in your feed. If their account is private, your follow request will need approval.
View your Followers and Following list from your profile. Unfollow anyone at any time. Remove followers if you prefer not to share your updates with them.

Connections are the backbone of your MissionPeak experience. They help you: Build your own network of outdoor companions. Discover new Huddles, Communities, and Inspirations. Grow your influence by sharing your journey with more people. tip Start by following a few Trailblazers (influencers and active community members) to get inspiration and discover exciting activities near you.
Connect MissionPeak to the health and fitness services you already use, so your activity data flows in automatically.

Devices & Services is where you manage connections between MissionPeak and outside health platforms. Once connected, MissionPeak can read activity data from these services to support features elsewhere in the app. Supported integrations: Apple Health (iOS) Google Health Connect (Android)

Activity Recording — imported workouts and activity data (like distance, duration, and route) can be used as recorded activities on MissionPeak. Challenges — progress toward a Challenge's goal can be calculated from data synced through Apple Health or Google Health Connect, in addition to activity recorded directly in the app.
documents.s: What connected data is used for

documents.t: Go to Settings > Devices & Services. Select Apple Health or Google Health Connect. Grant the requested permissions in the system prompt. Choose which data types to share with MissionPeak.

Revisit Settings > Devices & Services any time to review what's connected. Disconnect a service to stop new data from syncing. Previously imported activity and Challenge progress isn't removed automatically. You can also manage MissionPeak's permissions directly from the Apple Health or Google Health Connect app.
Skip manual entry — activity you've already recorded elsewhere counts automatically. Keep Challenge progress up to date across the apps you already use. Choose exactly which data types to share.
Connect Google Health Connect to bring your Android activity data into MissionPeak automatically.

The Google Health Connect integration lets MissionPeak read workout and activity data from Health Connect on Android. Once connected, activity recorded by other apps that sync to Health Connect can be used as a Record on MissionPeak.
documents.s: What is the Google Health Connect integration?

documents.t: Records — imported workouts (like distance, duration, and route where available) can be used as Records on MissionPeak. See About Records. Challenges — progress toward a Challenge's goal can be calculated from Health Connect data, in addition to activity recorded directly in the app. See About Challenges.
Go to Settings > Devices & Services. Select Google Health Connect. Grant the requested permissions in the Android system prompt. Choose which data types to share with MissionPeak.

Revisit Settings > Devices & Services any time to review what's connected. Disconnect Google Health Connect to stop new data from syncing. Previously imported activity and Challenge progress isn't removed automatically. You can also manage MissionPeak's permissions directly from the Health Connect app under App permissions.
documents.s: Managing or disconnecting Google Health Connect

documents.t: Skip manual entry — activity you've already recorded in other Android apps counts automatically. Keep Challenge progress up to date without opening a second app. Choose exactly which data types to share.

Huddles are at the heart of MissionPeak — they're the way you create, join, and enjoy social activities with like-minded people. Whether you're looking to organize a group hike, a casual meetup, or a structured activity, Huddles make it easy to bring people together.

A Huddle is a social event created by users on MissionPeak. It can be anything from a short walk in the park to a multi-day adventure, or even a virtual get-together. Each Huddle has its own details like date, time, venue, privacy level, and participant list. Think of Huddles as your personalized events board — simple to create, easy to join, and flexible for any type of activity.

Activity-based setup Choose from categories like General or Hiking. Activity-specific features are enabled automatically (e.g., trail details for Hiking). See About Activities for how a Huddle's activity type connects to recorded activity data. Event details & customization Add basic info: title, description, date, time, venue, and activity type. Optional details include an external URL, a custom RSVP start/end window, a meeting point, and a parking location. Privacy Options Control who can see or join: Public – open to everyone, including people you're not connected to. Unlisted – visible to anyone with the link, but won't appear in searches or lists. Connection – visible to friends/followers. Private – invite-only. Community – follows the privacy rules of the community hosting it. See Huddle Privacy Options for full details, including how privacy can be changed after a Huddle is created. Payment & Refund Hosts can mark a Huddle as free or paid, and set the attendance cost and refund policy. This is independent of Advanced Features and Advanced Settings. See Huddle Payments & Refunds for how paid Huddles work. Advanced Features Carpooling is currently the only Advanced Feature. A host can choose to enable it for a Huddle, letting participants coordinate rides and share costs. See About Carpools for details, including how Carpools can also be created independently of a Huddle. Advanced Settings A set of options including Decisive RSVPing, Require Approval, Attendee Limit, hiding the participant list, allowing participants to invite their connections, and allowing guests. See Huddle Advanced Settings for what each one does. Participant management Participants can send participation requests. If Require Approval is enabled (see Advanced Settings), requests go to a waiting list that the host or a co-host must manually approve or decline. Notifications Keep everyone updated with changes or reminders. Coordination via Messages Each Huddle has its own conversation so participants can coordinate details. See About Messages.

Tap the "+" menu in the app. Select Huddle. Fill in the event details – title, date, time, location, and activity type. Set privacy, and mark the Huddle as free or paid if applicable. Configure any Advanced Features (Carpooling) or Advanced Settings you want. Publish your Huddle and start inviting others.

Browse public Huddles on the Explore page or within your communities. Request to join if the Huddle requires approval. Get updates and reminders once you're added as a participant. Use built-in tools like carpooling to coordinate with others, if the host has enabled it.

Huddles make it simple to: Meet new people who share your interests. Plan outdoor activities without endless group chats. Keep all event details, logistics, and updates in one place. Build lasting connections through shared experiences.

On MissionPeak, Inspiration is more than just an article or blog post — it's your voice echoing across a community of outdoor explorers, wellness seekers, and changemakers. It's where your experience becomes someone else's motivation. Whether you're an adventurer, a health professional, or simply someone with a story to tell, Inspiration is your space to connect, uplift, and ignite action.

An Inspiration on MissionPeak is a thoughtfully written article, reflection, or guide shared with the community. It can be personal or professional, informative or reflective — but it always aims to educate, encourage, or empower others. Think of it as a mix of storytelling and resource-sharing, rooted in your unique outdoor or wellness journey. Inspiration posts are featured prominently in the MissionPeak feed and explore/discover pages, making them a great way to reach like-minded individuals.

MissionPeak encourages any passionate voice to contribute, especially: Outdoor Enthusiasts & Hikers: Share trail experiences, seasonal guides, hiking challenges, or beginner tips. Doctors, Physical Therapists, and Wellness Coaches: Educate the community on topics like injury prevention, hydration, recovery, mental health, or outdoor exercise benefits. Nutritionists & Lifestyle Experts: Provide advice on healthy snacking for day hikes, managing energy levels, or sustainable fitness habits. Parents & Working Professionals: Inspire others with stories about balancing a busy schedule with outdoor adventures. Group Organizers & Event Hosts: Reflect on group dynamics, safety tips, or the joy of shared outdoor moments. If you've ever had a moment of insight during a hike, a health transformation tied to nature, or an idea to make the outdoors more accessible — you have something worth sharing.

Here are a few Inspiration themes and ideas: "Why I Hike" — A personal journey of how nature helped your mental or physical health. "Beginner's Guide to [Trail Name or Activity]" — Tips and must-knows for newcomers. "How I Trained for [Challenge or Summit]" — Walk readers through your training journey. "Hiking with Kids" — Advice and encouragement for families hitting the trails. "My Favorite Bay Area Sunset Spots" — A curated list with photos or stories. "Post-Hike Recovery and Nutrition Tips" — From a professional or enthusiast perspective. "Outdoor Activities as a Tool for Burnout Recovery" — Based on real-life experience or medical insight. "Lessons from Leading 100 Hikes" — Group leadership and community-building reflections. You can also share seasonal inspirations, gear recommendations, trail safety tips, or even motivational thoughts for someone considering their first hike.

Everyone has a story. Yours could be the one that nudges someone off the couch, onto the trail, and into a better version of themselves. Use Inspiration on MissionPeak to start a ripple effect — one article, one idea, one life changed. Ready to write your own? See How to Write and Publish an Inspiration.
Messages let you talk directly with other MissionPeak users — to catch up with a Connection, coordinate a Huddle or Carpool, or join a topic-based discussion inside a Community.

Messages are how MissionPeak users communicate with each other. They come in a few forms: Direct messages — a private, one-on-one conversation between you and another user, similar to any messaging app. Group messages — a conversation with multiple friends at once, for chatting as a group outside of any specific Huddle, Carpool, or Community. Carpool messages — a conversation tied to a specific Carpool, so the driver and riders can coordinate pickup points, timing, and other details. Huddle messages — a conversation tied to a specific Huddle, so participants can plan logistics, share updates, and coordinate before and during the event. Community messages — topic-based conversations within a Community, letting members discuss specific subjects rather than one continuous group chat.

Direct messages Message any of your Connections one-on-one. Group messages Start a group conversation with multiple friends at once. Carpool messages Every Carpool has an associated conversation so drivers and riders can coordinate pickup details. See About Carpools. Huddle messages Every Huddle has an associated conversation for its participants to plan and coordinate. See About Huddles. Community messages Communities can host multiple topic-based discussions, so members can find and join the conversations relevant to them. See About Communities. Notifications Get notified about new messages, replies, and mentions.

Direct message — go to a Connection's profile or your Messages tab and start a new conversation. Group message — start a new conversation from your Messages tab and add friends to the group. Carpool message — open the Carpool and go to its conversation to message drivers and riders. Huddle message — open the Huddle and go to its conversation to message participants. Community message — open a Community and pick an existing topic, or start a new one (if allowed by the Community's settings).

Messages help you: Stay in touch with the people you're connected to. Coordinate the logistics of a Huddle or Carpool in one place. Have focused, topic-based conversations within a Community instead of one big feed.

Your Newsfeed is the central hub of MissionPeak. It's where you stay updated on everything happening in your network — Huddles, Communities, Inspirations, and updates from the people you follow. Think of it as your personal outdoor activity stream.

The Newsfeed is a live stream of posts, updates, and activities tailored to you. It combines content from: People you follow Communities you've joined Huddles you're part of Public posts and Inspirations from across MissionPeak This ensures you never miss out on new adventures, tips, or connections.

Posts – Short updates, photos, or check-ins from your connections. Inspirations – Stories, blogs, or articles written by members to inspire and guide others. Huddle updates – Announcements, reminders, and activity details from events you've joined or follow. Community highlights – New discussions or activities happening in your communities. Activity cards – Recorded activities (like hikes or runs) shared by users with maps, stats, and photos. See About Records.
documents.s: What You'll See in the Newsfeed

documents.t: Personalized updates See more of what matters — content from people and groups you're most connected with. Engagement options Like, comment, or share posts to interact with others. Build conversations and stay connected. Real-time sync As soon as your friends or communities post, it shows up in your feed. Content discovery Public Inspirations and activities may also appear, helping you find new people or groups.

Scroll to browse updates. Tap posts for more details (e.g., see the full Inspiration or join a Huddle). Engage with posts by liking or commenting. Follow links to Communities, Huddles, or profiles directly from the feed.

The Newsfeed helps you: Stay in touch with your friends and followers. Discover new activities and opportunities to join. Stay motivated through stories, posts, and Inspirations. Build a habit of outdoor activity by seeing what others are doing. tip For the best experience, follow active people and join vibrant communities — the more connections you make, the richer your Newsfeed becomes!
Records are how MissionPeak captures what you actually did outdoors — a hike, a run, a ride — so it can show up on your Newsfeed, count toward a Challenge, or attach to a Huddle.

A Record is the record of an activity you've recorded — a single session, like a hike or a run, with details such as distance, duration, and route. See About Activities for how activity types shape what gets recorded. Records can be created in two ways: Recorded in the app — start a recording directly in MissionPeak using your device's GPS. Synced from a connected service — imported automatically from Apple Health or Google Health Connect once connected. See About Devices & Services. However it's created, a Record can turn into an Activity Card — a Record shared to your Newsfeed with maps, stats, and photos.

In-app recording Start, pause, and finish a recording from the app, tracked live with GPS, to create a Record. Attach an activity type (e.g. Hiking, Running) to capture type-specific stats. Synced Records Activities recorded in Apple Health or Google Health Connect can sync in automatically as Records once connected. Sharing Choose to share a Record as an Activity Card on your Newsfeed, with maps, stats, and photos. Feeds other features Huddles — a Huddle's activity type can pull in relevant Record details, like trail info for a hike. Challenges — Records, whether created in-app or synced, can count toward a Challenge's goal.
Tap Record from the home screen. Choose an activity type. Start, pause, and finish the recording as you go. Review your stats and choose whether to share it as an Activity Card.

Records help you: Keep a personal history of what you've done outdoors. Share your activities with the MissionPeak community. Make progress toward Challenges automatically, whether created in-app or synced from a connected service.
If you no longer wish to use MissionPeak, you can permanently delete your account at any time. Deleting your account will remove your profile and all associated data from our platform.
documents.s: How to Permanently Delete Your Account

documents.t: To delete your account, follow these steps: Log in to your MissionPeak account (on web or mobile). Go to Settings from your profile menu. Select Account Deletion. Read the deletion warning carefully. Click Delete My Account and confirm your choice. warning This action is irreversible. Once your data is permanently deleted, it cannot be recovered.

Your account will be marked for deletion and scheduled for permanent removal in 30 days. You will be logged out immediately after confirming. All your content — including huddles, posts, messages, media, and profile information — will be permanently deleted after 30 days.
documents.s: What Happens After You Request Deletion

documents.t: If you change your mind during the 30-day window: Simply log back in using the same email or social login (Google, Facebook, Apple). Your deletion request will be automatically canceled, and your account will be restored.

Certain data, such as transaction records or invoices, may be retained if required by law (e.g., tax, legal, or fraud prevention purposes). All such data is handled in accordance with our Privacy Policy.
If you're facing any issues deleting your account or have further questions, please contact our support team at support@siddhatek.com.
When you create a Community on MissionPeak, you choose a privacy level that controls who can find it and who can see what's inside. You can set or change this from the Community's settings.
Anyone on MissionPeak can see posts, Huddles, and other items in this Community. The Community appears in search results and is visible on members' profiles.
Anyone on MissionPeak can find this Community and view its overview, but only members can see posts, Huddles, and other items in this Community.
Only Community members can see posts, Huddles, and other items in this Community.

Use Public if you want to grow your Community openly and make it easy for new people to discover and join. Use Protected if you want people to be able to find and learn about your Community before deciding to join, without exposing member activity. Use Private if your Community is meant for a specific, closed group — for example, a tight-knit friend group or an invite-only club.

Open the Community. Go to the Community's settings. Select Privacy. Choose a new privacy level. Save your changes. Changing privacy only affects visibility going forward — it doesn't notify members or remove anyone already in the Community.

The three levels form a scale from least to most restrictive: Public → Protected → Private. Community leaders can only move a Community to a more restrictive level, never a less restrictive one. This protects members who joined under the original privacy expectations. A Public Community can change to Protected or Private. A Protected Community can change to Private, but not back to Public. A Private Community cannot change to Protected or Public. If you need a more open Community, the best option is to create a new one at the privacy level you want, since loosening an existing Community's privacy isn't supported.
documents.s: Privacy can only move in one direction

documents.t: Huddles created within a Community can use the Community privacy option, which means the Huddle automatically follows whatever privacy level the Community is set to. See Huddle Privacy Options for details on all Huddle privacy settings.
documents.s: How this affects Huddles in a Community

documents.t: Answers to common questions about using MissionPeak.

What is MissionPeak?▾ MissionPeak is a dynamic platform designed to connect and inspire outdoor enthusiasts. Our mission is to empower individuals and communities by offering tools that promote adventure, wellness, and meaningful connections. With MissionPeak, you can discover a wide range of outdoor events, join vibrant communities, track your fitness goals, and draw inspiration from seasoned explorers. Who can benefit from using MissionPeak?▾ MissionPeak is for everyone — from experienced outdoor aficionados to those new to the world of exploration. The platform provides resources and communities that cater to all skill levels, ensuring that you can find events and groups that match your adventure style and personal goals. How do I get started with MissionPeak?▾ Getting started is easy! Download the MissionPeak app from your device's app store, sign up with your email or social media account, and personalize your profile. You can immediately begin exploring events, joining communities, and tracking your outdoor activities. What platforms is MissionPeak available on?▾ MissionPeak is available as a mobile app for iOS and Android. Some features, like browsing public content, may also be accessible from a web browser. Check your device's app store for the latest version and supported operating system requirements. Do I need to create an account to use MissionPeak?▾ You can view some general, public information without an account, but creating a free account is required to join Huddles, participate in Communities, track activities, or publish Inspirations. Signing up only takes a couple of minutes with an email address or a supported social login. Can non-members view the events and activities offered by MissionPeak?▾ While non-members can view general information about MissionPeak, access to detailed event information, participation, and community features typically requires creating an account. This ensures a secure and personalized experience for all users.

How can I discover events and activities using the app?▾ The MissionPeak app features a user-friendly interface where you can browse and filter events based on your preferences, location, and interests. Whether you're interested in hiking, camping, or other outdoor activities, the app offers a comprehensive list of events that you can join. You can also receive personalized recommendations tailored to your past activities and preferences. What's the difference between a Huddle and a Community?▾ A Huddle is a single planned activity — like a Saturday hike or a one-time meetup — with its own date, location, and participant list. A Community is an ongoing group built around a shared interest, where members can post updates, share Inspirations, and organize multiple Huddles over time. Think of a Community as the group, and a Huddle as one event that group might run. How does the community feature work?▾ Our app enables users to connect with like-minded individuals by joining or creating communities. You can participate in group discussions, share photos and stories, and organize events with peers who share your passion for the outdoors. These communities foster collaboration and allow you to build friendships based on shared interests and outdoor experiences. What fitness tracking features are available?▾ MissionPeak integrates cutting-edge fitness tracking tools that help you monitor your activity levels and achievements. Track metrics like distance hiked, elevation gained, calories burned, and more. You can set personal goals, view progress reports, and celebrate milestones, all within the app. This feature helps you stay motivated and engaged on your fitness journey. Does MissionPeak work without an internet connection during a hike?▾ Core features like Huddles, Communities, and the Newsfeed require an internet connection to stay in sync. If you're heading somewhere with limited signal, it's a good idea to download any trail details or maps you need in advance and double-check meeting details before you lose connectivity. How can I get inspiration from trailblazers and influencers?▾ Within the app, you'll find curated content from renowned trailblazers and influencers who share their experiences, tips, and breathtaking stories from their outdoor adventures. These narratives are designed to motivate you, provide practical advice, and introduce you to new ways of exploring the natural world. Can I organize my own events through MissionPeak?▾ Yes, you can organize and manage your own events within the MissionPeak app. Whether it's a group hike, camping trip, or a community meetup, you can create an event, set the details, and invite other members to join. This feature helps to bring together fellow adventurers and foster strong community bonds. What kind of content can I share in the app?▾ Users can share various content types including photos, videos, and written posts about their outdoor experiences. Whether you're documenting your latest hike or sharing tips on gear, MissionPeak provides a platform for creative expression and knowledge sharing among enthusiasts. Can I connect my fitness devices to the MissionPeak app?▾ Yes, the app is designed to be compatible with a variety of popular fitness devices and apps, allowing you to seamlessly integrate your fitness data. This way, you can ensure all your activity statistics are consolidated in one place for easier tracking and analysis. Are there any incentives for sharing my outdoor achievements?▾ MissionPeak may offer features like virtual badges, challenges, and leaderboards to encourage sharing and enhance user engagement. By participating in these features, you can earn recognition within the community and motivate others by showcasing your accomplishments. How do I participate in challenges or competitions?▾ The MissionPeak app periodically hosts challenges and competitions that you can join. Simply access the "Challenges" section in the app to find current opportunities, register for those that interest you, and track your progress directly within the app.

How is personal data managed and protected on MissionPeak?▾ MissionPeak is committed to protecting your privacy and personal data. We use robust security protocols to safeguard user information and comply with applicable data protection laws. You can find detailed information in our Privacy Policy, accessible via the app and our website. How do I update my account information or change my password?▾ You can update your profile details, email, and password at any time from the Settings menu in the app. If you signed up using a social login (Google, Facebook, or Apple), password changes are managed through that provider instead. Can I change my username or date of birth?▾ No, usernames and dates of birth cannot be changed directly in the app, as both are used to keep accounts secure and verify age-appropriate access to certain features. If your date of birth was entered incorrectly at sign-up, email support@siddhatek.com with a government-issued photo ID showing your correct date of birth, and our team will verify it and update your account. See Changing Your Username or Date of Birth for details. Who can see my posts, activities, and Inspirations?▾ That depends on the privacy settings you choose for your account and for each individual Huddle, Community, or Inspiration. Content marked Public can be seen by anyone, while Connection- or Private-level content is limited to your followers or approved members. You can adjust these settings at any time. Can I make my profile, Huddles, or Communities private?▾ Yes. Huddles and Communities each support privacy levels ranging from fully public to invite-only, and your personal account has its own privacy controls for who can follow you or see your activity. See Huddle Privacy Options and Community Privacy Options for the specific privacy options available for each.

Is there a cost to join MissionPeak?▾ MissionPeak offers a range of services for free, allowing you to explore many of its features without any cost. For those seeking an enhanced experience, premium memberships may be available which offer additional benefits such as exclusive events, advanced tracking features, and more personalized content. Check the app for specific details on pricing and features. What's included in a free account versus a premium membership?▾ A free account gives you access to the core MissionPeak experience — joining Huddles and Communities, tracking activities, and following Connections. Premium memberships, where available, may add benefits like advanced tracking, exclusive events, or additional personalization. Specific premium features and pricing are shown in the app, since they may vary by region or change over time. How do I manage or cancel a premium subscription?▾ Subscriptions are managed through the app store you subscribed through (Apple App Store or Google Play). Open your device's subscription settings to view, change, or cancel a MissionPeak subscription. If you need help locating it, our Support Center can point you in the right direction. Does MissionPeak charge for attending a Huddle?▾ That depends on the Huddle — a host can mark their Huddle as free or paid. For paid Huddles, the host (not MissionPeak) sets the attendance cost, and payment is made directly to the host in cash or another external method the two of you arrange. See Huddle Payments & Refunds for details. Can I get a refund for a paid Huddle?▾ Refunds for Huddle attendance are set by the host, not MissionPeak. If a host's refund policy says "no refunds," or if no refund policy is listed at all, no refund will be provided. Always check a Huddle's listed cost and refund policy, and confirm directly with the host, before paying. See Huddle Payments & Refunds for how this works.

How can I contact support if I have issues?▾ Our dedicated support team is ready to assist you with any app-related questions or concerns. Access the "Contact Us" section in the app to reach our support center, where you can find FAQs, troubleshooting guides, or submit a request for direct assistance. How does MissionPeak ensure user safety during events?▾ Safety is a top priority for MissionPeak. While the app provides information about events, each user is encouraged to follow safety guidelines and prepare accordingly. We offer resources and tips on safe practices in the outdoors, and we encourage event organizers to include safety information in their event descriptions. How do I report inappropriate content or behavior?▾ If you come across content or behavior that violates our community standards, use the report option available on the post, profile, Huddle, or Community in question. Our team reviews reports and takes action in line with our Acceptable Use Policy.

How do the Influencer partnerships work on MissionPeak?▾ MissionPeak collaborates with outdoor influencers who provide expert insights, tips, and motivational content. These partnerships are meant to enrich the user's experience by providing authentic, value-driven content that resonates with the outdoor community. How can businesses collaborate with or sponsor MissionPeak events?▾ Businesses can collaborate with MissionPeak by sponsoring events, offering products for community challenges, or employing advertising within the app. Interested businesses can contact our partnership team through the "Business Solutions" section on our website or app to explore opportunities.
Common terms you'll come across while using MissionPeak, defined in one place.

Your personal MissionPeak profile. A free account is required to join Huddles, participate in Communities, track activities, or publish Inspirations. See How to Permanently Delete Your Account for account management details.
A Record — like a hike or run — shared to the Newsfeed with maps, stats, and photos. See About Records.

The kind of outdoor activity something on MissionPeak is centered around — like General or Hiking. Activity type shapes Huddle features, recorded stats, and some Challenge goals. See About Activities.
Your AI-powered outdoor companion built into MissionPeak. Aurora answers questions, recommends activities, and helps with planning Huddles or drafting Inspirations. See About Aurora.
A Huddle feature that lets participants coordinate rides and share costs for getting to an event.

An ongoing group built around a shared interest, where members post updates, share Inspirations, and organize multiple Huddles over time. Communities can be Public, Protected (discoverable, but content limited to members), or Private (content limited to members, invite-only). See About Communities and Community Privacy Options.
The relationship between you and another user — formed by following or being followed. Connections shape what appears in your Newsfeed. See About Connections.

A Follower is someone who follows you and sees your shareable posts, Huddles, and Inspirations. Following refers to the people you've chosen to follow, whose activity appears in your feed. See About Connections.

A single planned activity — like a Saturday hike or a one-time meetup — with its own date, location, privacy level, and participant list. Huddles can be Public, Unlisted (visible via link only), Connection-visible, Private (invite-only), or tied to a Community's privacy rules. See About Huddles and Huddle Privacy Options.

A written article, story, or guide shared with the MissionPeak community — part storytelling, part resource-sharing, rooted in an outdoor or wellness journey. See About Inspirations and How to Write and Publish an Inspiration.
A conversation between MissionPeak users — either a direct message, a Huddle/Carpool coordination thread, or a topic-based discussion within a Community. See About Messages.
Your personalized activity stream, combining posts, Inspirations, and updates from the people you follow, the Communities you've joined, and the Huddles you're part of. See About Newsfeed.

The record of an activity you've recorded on MissionPeak — like a hike or a run — created either in the app or synced from a connected service like Apple Health or Google Health Connect. A Record can be shared to the Newsfeed as an Activity Card and can count toward Challenge progress. See About Records.
A Huddle tool for building and coordinating tasks among participants — for example, dividing up what everyone brings to an event.

An active community member or outdoor influencer whose experiences, tips, and stories appear throughout MissionPeak to motivate and guide others. Don't see a term you're looking for? Check the FAQ or email us at support@siddhatek.com.

When creating a Huddle, hosts can configure a set of Advanced Settings that control how participants RSVP, how many people can join, and what other participants can see or do. These are separate from Advanced Features (currently just Carpooling) and from a Huddle's payment and refund details.
If enabled, participants must choose either Attend or Not Attend when responding to the Huddle — there is no maybe/tentative option. This is useful for hosts who need a firm headcount.

If enabled, participants who request to join are placed on a waiting list instead of being added immediately. The host (or a co-host) must manually approve or decline each participation request. If this setting is off, participants who request to join (or who are allowed to join directly, depending on the Huddle's privacy level) are added without manual review.
Lets a host cap how many participants can join the Huddle. When enabled, the host enters a maximum number of attendees; once that limit is reached, no further participants can join.
Controls whether the participant list is visible to other participants. The host and any co-hosts can always see the full participant list — this setting only affects what other participants can see.

Controls whether participants (not just the host) can invite their own connections to the Huddle. If enabled, participants can bring in new people who weren't part of the original invite or audience — useful for organically growing a Huddle. If disabled, only the host controls who can be added beyond the Huddle's normal privacy/audience rules.
documents.s: Allow Participant to Invite Their Connections

documents.t: Controls whether participants can bring guests with them to the Huddle, in addition to RSVPing themselves.

Advanced Settings appear on the Huddle creation screen, separate from Advanced Features (Carpooling) and from the Huddle's free/paid and refund policy settings. See About Huddles for an overview of all the options available when creating a Huddle, and Huddle Payments & Refunds for payment-specific details.

Attending a Huddle can be free or paid, depending on how the host sets it up. This article explains how paid Huddles work on MissionPeak, how payments and refunds are handled, and what to expect as a host or an attendee.

When creating a Huddle, the host decides whether attendance is free or paid. This is set as part of the Huddle's advanced options when the Huddle is created. Free Huddles have no attendance cost — anyone who joins can attend at no charge. Paid Huddles require attendees to pay a cost set by the host in order to attend.

MissionPeak does not set, collect, or process attendance costs. For paid Huddles, the host — not MissionPeak — is responsible for: Deciding the attendance cost. Deciding the refund policy (for example, whether refunds are offered if an attendee cancels, or if the Huddle is changed or canceled). If a host sets no refund policy, that means no refunds will be provided under any circumstance. If a host doesn't set a refund policy at all, this is treated the same as "no refunds" — no refund policy stated means no refund will be provided. Attendees should check a Huddle's listed cost and refund policy before requesting to join, and should confirm both directly with the host before paying. Huddle details are entered by the host, and MissionPeak does not verify or guarantee their accuracy.
documents.s: Who sets the cost and refund policy

documents.t: The only currency currently supported for Huddle attendance costs is US Dollars (USD).

MissionPeak currently supports one payment method for paid Huddles: Direct, Cash or External. This means: Payment is made directly to the host — not through MissionPeak. Payment can be made in cash or through any other external method the host and attendee agree on (for example, a payment app, bank transfer, or other arrangement outside of MissionPeak). MissionPeak does not facilitate, collect, hold, or transmit any payment between attendees and hosts.
documents.s: How payment works: Direct, Cash or External

documents.t: If a refund is due — whether because of the host's refund policy, a canceled Huddle, or any other reason — the refund is handled the same way as payment: directly between the host and the attendee, outside of MissionPeak. MissionPeak does not process, issue, or guarantee refunds for Huddle attendance.

MissionPeak provides the platform for hosts to list a Huddle's cost and for attendees to see that information before joining. MissionPeak is not involved in, and assumes no responsibility for, any payment or refund made between a host and an attendee, including: Collecting or processing payments. Resolving payment disputes. Issuing or enforcing refunds. Hosts and attendees are responsible for agreeing on payment and refund terms directly with each other.

Hosts: Clearly state the attendance cost, payment method expectations, and refund policy in your Huddle details before attendees join. Attendees: Review the listed cost and refund policy before requesting to join a paid Huddle, and confirm payment details directly with the host. Both: Keep your own records of any payments or refunds made outside of MissionPeak, since MissionPeak does not track or store payment transactions.

Every Huddle you create on MissionPeak has a privacy setting that controls who can see it, who can find it, and who can RSVP or participate. You choose this when creating the Huddle, and can adjust it from the Huddle's settings.

The Huddle will be visible to anyone on MissionPeak, including people who are not directly connected to you. It will appear in searches on the platform, and anyone can view the Huddle details, RSVP, and share it with others.
Anyone with the link can view the Huddle details, RSVP, and interact with the Huddle. It will not appear in MissionPeak searches or Huddle lists unless the user participates.
The Huddle will only be visible to people within your network or those you are connected to. Only your connections can view the Huddle details, RSVP, and interact with the Huddle.
The Huddle will only be visible to the people you invite. Huddle details are not shared publicly or with your connections. Only invited guests can view the Huddle, RSVP, and participate.
Privacy of Huddles hosted in a Community is controlled by the privacy setting of the Community. See Community Privacy Options for how Public, Protected, and Private Communities affect visibility.

Use Public to reach the widest audience and let anyone discover and join. Use Unlisted to share a Huddle only with people you send the link to, without it showing up in search. Use Connection to keep a Huddle within your existing network. Use Private for invite-only gatherings where you control the exact guest list. Use Community when the Huddle belongs to a Community and should automatically follow that Community's privacy rules.

Open the Huddle. Go to the Huddle's settings. Select Privacy. Choose a new privacy level. Save your changes. Changing privacy only affects visibility going forward — it doesn't notify existing participants or remove anyone already RSVP'd.

The four levels form a scale from least to most restrictive: Public → Unlisted → Connection → Private. Hosts can only move a Huddle to a more restrictive level, never a less restrictive one, to protect the expectations of people who already RSVP'd or were invited. A Public Huddle can change to Unlisted, Connection, or Private. An Unlisted Huddle can change to Connection or Private, but not back to Public. A Connection Huddle can change to Private, but not back to Unlisted or Public. A Private Huddle cannot change to Connection, Unlisted, or Public. If you need a more open Huddle, create a new one at the privacy level you want — loosening an existing Huddle's privacy isn't supported.
documents.s: Privacy can only move in one direction

documents.t: To keep MissionPeak safe and trustworthy for everyone, usernames and dates of birth cannot be changed directly from the app or website. This helps us maintain accurate identity records and prevent misuse of the platform.
documents.s: Changing Your Username or Date of Birth

documents.t: Username is used as a stable identifier across your profile, posts, huddles, and connections. Allowing frequent changes could cause confusion or be used to impersonate other members. Date of birth is used to verify age-appropriate access to certain features. It's locked to prevent users from altering it to bypass age restrictions.

If your date of birth was entered incorrectly during sign-up, we can correct it — but we need to verify your identity first. To request a correction: Email our support team at support@siddhatek.com with the subject line "Date of Birth Correction Request". Attach a clear photo or scan of a government-issued photo ID (such as a passport, driver's license, or national ID card) that shows your correct date of birth. Include the email address or username associated with your MissionPeak account. warning Make sure your ID is clearly legible and matches the name on your MissionPeak account. Requests without valid proof cannot be processed. Our team will review your request, verify the document, and update your date of birth once confirmed.
documents.s: Requesting a Date of Birth Correction

documents.t: Username changes are not available through self-service. If you believe there is an exceptional reason your username needs to change (for example, impersonation or a safety concern), contact our support team at support@siddhatek.com with details, and we'll review it on a case-by-case basis.
Any identity document you share with us is used only to verify your request and is handled in accordance with our Privacy Policy. It is not shared publicly or displayed on your profile.
If you have questions about this process, please contact our support team at support@siddhatek.com.

Inspiration on MissionPeak is your way to share stories, hiking experiences, expert advice, or wellness journeys with the outdoor community. Whether you're a weekend hiker, nature lover, or health professional, your words can inspire and influence others. Here's a step-by-step guide to help you create and publish your first Inspiration.
documents.s: How to Write and Publish an Inspiration

documents.t: Visit missionpeak.app Create a free account or log in if you already have one
documents.s: Step 1: Sign Up and Log In

documents.t: There are two ways to begin: Go to Inspiration > My Inspirations and click the Create button, OR Click the "+" (Plus) menu in the top-right Appbar and select Inspiration

Enter a compelling title Write your content using the rich text editor — feel free to format headings, lists, and quotes Upload a cover photo to make your post visually engaging Add a caption and photo credit if needed tip Stories with images get more attention and engagement.
Click Next to preview your post Review the layout, content, and visual feel If changes are needed, click Back to return to editing mode

Add a snippet (SEO description) to improve discoverability in search engines Select: Primary category (required) Secondary category (optional) Primary activity (e.g., Hiking, Yoga – if relevant) Secondary activity (optional) Enable or disable commenting (enabled by default) Set visibility: Public: Visible to all Unlisted: Only accessible via direct link Private: Only you can view Add up to 5 topic tags for better reach and categorization
Ready to go? Click Publish Want to time it right? Schedule the inspiration by choosing your desired date and time
Congratulations! Your inspiration is now published and visible to your selected audience. You can view and manage all your posts under Inspiration > My Inspirations.

By sharing your inspirations, you can: Motivate others to explore the outdoors Offer health tips or trail advice Establish your presence as a thought leader in the community If you have any questions or need help, feel free to reach out to us at support@siddhatek.com.
documents.s: Become a Voice in the Community
